Hi all —

Quick technical summary from the infra/security side — happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through this. TL;DR: we can support the RTBF scope you described, but there are constraints and measurable timelines for backups/snapshots that we should explicitly call out to FinServCorp.

Primary deletion path (normal flow):
- Mark record(s) for deletion in the control plane and enqueue for immediate purge from primary stores (databases + object stores).
- Inference caches (KV cache/prefix cache): evicted asynchronously; we will flush matching keys on request.
- Embeddings: stored as objects/rows tied to account IDs — these are deleted in the same purge.
- Logs: we segment logs by request-id and account id. PII in logs is redacted by default; anything user-supplied content can be purged on request.

Backups / snapshots (important limitations):
- Managed snapshots: cloud provider snapshots are immutable and may persist beyond primary deletion. Our standard practice: we track backup retention windows and run a retention-based purge cycle. For most providers, final physical removal can take up to 30 days after snapshot expiration, but that depends on provider dedupe and cross-region replication.
- Long-term archives / cold storage: if data is archived to cold storage (rare for customer inference data), purge can be longer (30–90 days) depending on vendor contracts.
- Recommendation: we propose a contractual maximum window of 90 days for complete removal from backups/archives, with interim attestations at 7/30/90 days. We can provide logs of retention jobs and confirmation artifacts.

Other notes:
- We do not retrain public models with customer private data by default; any fine-tuning jobs would require a separate opt-in and explicit data usage clause.
- For auditability, we can provide a deletion manifest (list of object keys/IDs removed) and the job run IDs that performed purging.

Next steps I recommend we offer to FinServCorp:
1) Show them the proposed delete SLA language (I’ll draft a paragraph we can insert into the SOW).
2) Offer a 30/90-day phased deletion commitment: immediate purge from primary stores, 30-day confirmation of backup purge progress, final attestation at 90 days for any cold storage.
3) Provide SOC2 audit excerpt and our data-retention policy (attached).

I’ll attach the redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf for their legal team.
